**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity), clause 3.4 (p0022).**

The planner flagged this rule as likely absent, but a records-inspection right does exist — clause 3.4 in the payments section, which I located by searching for "inspect"/"records" rather than "audit".

**How it scores against the playbook:**

| Term | Clause 3.4 | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Notice | 30 days' prior written | Meets preferred |
| Timing | Company's normal business hours | Meets preferred |
| Scope | Payment-calculation records only | Meets preferred |
| Cost | Borne by HDI, unconditionally | Beats preferred (no 5% carve-out) |
| System access | None | Meets preferred |
| **Frequency** | **No limit** | **Fails preferred and fallback** |

The absence of any frequency cap is the single material gap — an uncapped right edges toward the walk-away position on unlimited audits. Since every other material term already sits at or above preferred, the redline is a single minimal insertion: "not more than once in any twelve (12) month period."

Two shortfalls I deliberately did **not** flag, per the rule that minor sub-elements belong in the rationale: the inspector is HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor, and confidentiality isn't restated in 3.4 — though I confirmed clause 8.2 already binds HDI to hold Company Confidential Information in strict confidence, so the protection is not actually absent.
